hello.note: Formal, safe with anyone, including strangers and elders.

slang.note: Casual hi, used with friends, peers, and younger people.

good_evening.note: Naabig is the Zurich-dialect shortening of Abend.

goodbye.note: Literally 'until we see each other again'; polite and all-purpose.

slang.note: Casual, Italian-influenced; fine with friends, less so at work.

how_are_you.note: Polite form for someone you don't know; casual: Wie gaht's dir?

thank_you.note: Merci alone also works; vilmal ('many times') adds warmth.

excuse_me.note: Zurich-dialect softening of the French excusez; light and friendly.

slang.note: Peer slang like 'Amazing, dude!'; Alte suits a woman or mixed group, Alter a man, Aute is the Bernese spelling. Best with people near your own age.

delicious.note: Said about food you're enjoying; 'Das isch fein' means 'that's tasty.'

cheers.note: Meet people's eyes as you clink glasses, per Swiss custom.

slang.note: Cute diminutive; extra warm and casual, used with friends.
